scenario.name: NCSC-NL, Red Hat & MITRE DFIR — Linux /etc/ld.so.preload Userland Rootkit & /proc/1/maps Forensics
scenario.overview: Imagine an invisible tailor sneaking into a factory dressing room and sewing a rigged lining into the universal work coat hanging on the entrance rack. Every factory inspector who slips on a standard coat automatically sees blurred lenses that hide the tailor hidden doorway, until a forensic auditor arrives with sealed, self-contained binoculars from outside the factory and reads the raw room occupancy ledger directly. In this scenario (T1574.006, NCSC-NL, Red Hat & MITRE DFIR, Linux /etc/ld.so.preload Userland Rootkit & /proc/1/maps Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: shared Library Compilation, then global Dynamic Linker Injection, then forensic Detection via /proc/1/maps. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Shared Library Compilation, then Global Dynamic Linker Injection, then Forensic Detection via /proc/1/maps, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on auditd Event 257 correlated across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Shared Library Compilation & /etc/ld.so.preload Registration (auditd nametype=CREATE)
stages.subtitle: Persistence (T1574.006 - Hijack Execution Flow: Dynamic Linker Hijacking)
stages.description: Under cover of night, the tailor slips a custom rigged coat lining into the supply shelf and writes its tag number onto the mandatory entrance-rack sheet. Even though the front-desk tools will soon be fooled, the tamper-proof security camera bolted above the rack records the exact moment the sheet is edited. The actor places a malicious ELF shared object at /usr/lib64/libudev-guardian.so and writes its path into /etc/ld.so.preload. stages.title: Stage 2: Global Dynamic Linker Injection & Userland PLT/GOT Hooking of readdir64() and fopen()
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1014 - Rootkit: Userland libc Function Hooking)
stages.description: Every time a normal factory worker starts a routine floor check, the entrance dresser hands them the rigged coat first. Inside each worker goggles, the rigged lining intercepts every glance down the aisles and every glance at the attendance clipboard, erasing the intruder files and connections before the worker eyes can read them. On every subsequent execution of a dynamically linked binary (such as ps, ls, netstat, or lsof), /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 reads /etc/ld.so.preload and maps libudev-guardian.so before libc.so.6. The library overrides readdir64() and fopen("/proc/net/tcp") via dlsym(RTLD_NEXT...) so standard userland tools hide the rootkit’s files, PIDs, and network connections, including hiding /etc/ld.so.preload itself (logged in Linux Audit Event 9 with DynamicLinker=/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2, InjectedIntoProcess=/usr/bin/ps, /usr/bin/ls, /usr/bin/ss, HookMechanism=dlsym, RTLD_NEXT overriding libc readdir64/fopen so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). steps.plainTitle: Global Dynamic Linker Injection & Userland PLT/GOT Hooking of readdir64() and fopen()
steps.storyAnalogy: Every time a normal factory worker starts a routine floor check, the entrance dresser hands them the rigged coat first. steps.plainTitle: Forensic Detection via /proc/1/maps, /proc/self/map_files & Statically Linked Busybox
steps.storyAnalogy: Refusing to put on any factory coat at all, the forensic auditor walks in wearing completely self-contained outside gear and reads the raw hallway map posted inside the master guard station, immediately spotting the foreign rigged lining wrapped around every single worker in the building.
steps.simpleExplanation: During DFIR triage, the analyst bypasses userland libc hooks by inspecting /proc/1/maps (or /proc/self/maps via a shell builtin read loop) and running a statically linked busybox binary (which does not use ld-linux.so and is immune to /etc/ld.so.preload).
